prompt: State how a concurrent writer would invalidate a stronger transactional-snapshot claim.
answer: Validation and copying are separate reads of caller-owned mutable storage. A concurrent writer could change values after validation or during copying, so a returned array might reflect different logical versions or values not covered by the earlier check. Independence after return does not make the capture linearizable or transactional. A stronger design needs a shared ownership/locking protocol covering validation plus copy and respected by every writer, or an immutable/versioned source snapshot with a reviewed consistency protocol. Copying or setting only one view read-only does not by itself exclude all writers. No live concurrent-writer experiment or synchronization implementation was executed.
